correctness.rationale: Order preservation and the explicit branch solutions delimit the two periodic half-lines exactly. The two total integrals vanish by summing period translates of the coefficient, and the equality of half-period primitives follows by orthogonality of sin t to all harmonics in sinh((ε/k)sin kt). All other orbits cross once each way, transversely, on the two open half-periods. For upward phase t and reflected downward phase r, the positive branch gives A(t)=B(r). The negative branches give ρ=−B(t), P(ρ)=−A(r), so at a fixed point A(t)+B(t)=A(r)+B(r). Strict monotonicity yields r=t, and conversely A(t)=B(t) gives a fixed point. As an independent upper bound, A−B vanishes at both endpoints and (A−B)'=−2 sinh((ε/k)sin kt) sin t has exactly k−1 interior zeros for ε≠0, so Rolle gives at most k−2 interior fixed points. The frozen proof's stronger displacement-critical-point census also works: the endpoint deficits vanish quadratically with positive smooth factors, making the inverse composition C¹-close to the identity up to both endpoints; the exact variational multiplier is exp((2ε/k)[sin(kt₂)−sin(kt₁)]), therefore the displacement-critical-point equation converges in C¹ to 2sin kt with pinned simple endpoints. For the lower bound, the transverse branch solutions depend smoothly on initial value and ε on interior compact sets. Splitting the first-order displacement at θ=arccos(ρ+1) and integrating by parts gives (4/k)∫₀^θ sin(kt)sin t dt, equal to the stated positive weight times T_k''; Rolle and the degree prove k−2 simple roots. Their continuations for either sign of nonzero ε have P'≠1, hence are hyperbolic, and exhaust the upper bound (including zero cycles at k=2).
residual_risks: Smallness for the exact hyperbolic census is for fixed k. Poincaré-map critical points here mean zeros of (P−id)' on the open crossing interval; on the fixed half-lines the displacement is constant.

value.rationale: This well-known example is used to force degree dependence in global cycle bounds. Upgrading its lower bound to an exact isolated-cycle count, including the two grazing edges where compact perturbation theory is not decisive, resolves a concrete gap. The exact branch correspondence also distinguishes isolated hyperbolic cycles from the continuous fixed families.
residual_risks: No bound uniform in k or claim of a global center or general Hilbert-number formula.
